final_message:
I changed rule 2 in `skills/log-redaction/SKILL.md`, but I can't tell you it's ready to ship, because I haven't tested it. I only have file tools in this session, so I couldn't run any subagent scenarios.

The new text is: "Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included."

I don't think this is only a wording fix. The old rule said agents "should" redact "API tokens". The new one says "must" redact "every token, key and password" in "every log line", debug logs included. That widens the scope from API tokens to keys and passwords, and it covers debug logs, which the old text never mentioned. It also turns a "should" into a "must". Agents could behave differently after this change, for example by redacting passwords they used to log or by redacting in debug prints they used to leave alone. The skill's own rules require a guard run for any edit, even a "wording fix". A guard run means running the relevant cases on the old text and the new text, and shipping only if no case gets worse. Last month's untested fix not breaking anything doesn't tell us much about this one.

Before you cut the release, I'd run these cases on the old text and the new text:
- A debug `print` that dumps a dict containing a password.
- A request logger that includes an API key header.
- An INFO line carrying a bearer token, to check that the existing `[REDACTED]` format still gets used.
- A case that has nothing sensitive, to check that agents don't over-redact request ids and routes (rule 1).

If you want to ship now anyway, that's your decision. The edit is a single line in git, so `git checkout skills/log-redaction/SKILL.md` undoes it. I'd describe it in the release notes as a scope change, not a wording fix. I can write up these scenarios as a test kit if you'd like.

input.old_string: 2. Agents should redact API tokens from log lines.
input.new_string: 2. Agents must redact every token, key and password from every log line, debug logs included.
